prompts.display_text: Pin the Sacred Grove, site of the First Vision in 1820.
prompts.text_original: Drop a pin on the Sacred Grove near Palmyra, New York, where Joseph Smith prayed in the spring of 1820.

place.name: Sacred Grove (Smith Family Farm), Palmyra, New York

prompts.citation: Sacred Grove Historic Site page, ChurchofJesusChrist.org, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: On a spring day in 1820, 14-year-old Joseph Smith went alone to a grove near his family's farm to pray. God the Father and Jesus Christ appeared to him, an event called the First Vision. The Smith family farm nearby is also where the angel Moroni first visited Joseph in 1823.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country outside the US with City in a temple name. Mexico City is the easy one.
prompts.text_original: A country outside the United States with a temple (any stage, as of November 2026) whose official name includes the word "City".
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronology cross-checked with the Church's official temple list, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: Some temple names include the word City because the city itself does. Outside the US these include Mexico City, Guatemala City and Cebu City.

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: Mexico City Mexico (dedicated 1983); Mexico City Benemérito Mexico (announced).

answers.name: Guatemala
answers.fact: Guatemala City Guatemala (dedicated 1984); Miraflores Guatemala City Guatemala (dedicated 2026).

answers.name: Panama
answers.fact: Panama City Panama (dedicated 2008).

answers.name: Philippines
answers.fact: Cebu City Philippines (dedicated 2010); Tacloban City Philippines (under construction); Tuguegarao City Philippines (announced).

answers.name: Argentina
answers.fact: Buenos Aires City Center Argentina (announced).

answers.name: Nigeria
answers.fact: Benin City Nigeria (under construction).

prompts.display_text: Pin a South Pacific country or territory President David O. McKay visited on his 1955 tour.
prompts.text_original: In January and February 1955, David O. McKay became the first Church president to tour the South Pacific missions, choosing a temple site in New Zealand along the way. Pin a South Pacific country or territory he visited on that tour.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies; Church newsroom; Ensign Dec. 1998
prompts.note: Hawaii counts as USA but lies in the North Pacific, so it is outside this South Pacific prompt.
prompts.summary: Early in 1955, President David O. McKay and his wife, Emma Ray, flew through the South Pacific, meeting Saints in Fiji, Tonga, both Samoas, the Cook Islands and Tahiti before visiting New Zealand and Australia. In New Zealand he quietly chose the hill near Hamilton where the first temple in the Southern Hemisphere would rise.

answers.name: Australia
answers.fact: First Church president to visit Australia, 1955.

answers.name: New Zealand
answers.fact: Visited the Hamilton college project and chose the temple site; announced Feb. 17, 1955.

answers.name: Tonga
answers.fact: Visited Tongatapu and Vava'u and spoke of a future temple.

answers.name: Samoa
answers.fact: Met Saints in Pesega and Sauniatu, January 14-17, 1955.

answers.name: American Samoa
answers.fact: Met Saints in Pago Pago and Mapusaga, January 14, 1955.

answers.name: Fiji
answers.fact: Spoke to Saints in Suva, January 9, 1955.

answers.name: French Polynesia
answers.fact: First Church president to visit Tahiti, January 18-20, 1955.

answers.name: Cook Islands
answers.fact: Held a one-hour meeting with 66 members at Aitutaki while his plane refueled.

prompts.display_text: Pin a land Russell M. Nelson dedicated for the preaching of the gospel while an Apostle.
prompts.text_original: A country Russell M. Nelson, while serving in the Quorum of the Twelve, dedicated or rededicated for the preaching of the gospel.
prompts.citation: Church History Department, Global Histories country chronologies, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: As a member of the Twelve, Russell M. Nelson offered prayers dedicating many nations for the preaching of the gospel. Several came in early 1990, just weeks after communist rule ended in Eastern Europe, and others followed in Africa, Central America and the Pacific.

answers.name: Bulgaria
answers.fact: February 13, 1990, Sofia: dedicated Bulgaria for the preaching of the gospel.

answers.name: Czech Republic
answers.fact: February 6, 1990, Prague: rededicated Czechoslovakia for the preaching of the gospel.

answers.name: Romania
answers.fact: February 8, 1990, Bucharest: dedicated Romania in Cismigiu Park, weeks after the Romanian Revolution.

answers.name: Estonia
answers.fact: April 25, 1990, Tallinn: dedicated Estonia above the Lauluvaljak amphitheater.

answers.name: Honduras
answers.fact: 1991, Tegucigalpa: dedicated Honduras on the mountain El Picacho.

answers.name: El Salvador
answers.fact: April 7, 1990, San Salvador: dedicated El Salvador for the preaching of the gospel.

answers.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
answers.fact: September 8, 2010, Sarajevo: dedicated the country at Vraca Memorial Park.

answers.name: Namibia
answers.fact: August 22, 1992, Windhoek: dedicated Namibia for the preaching of the restored gospel.

answers.name: French Polynesia
answers.fact: 1994, Papeete: dedicated the country at the 150th anniversary of the Church there.

answers.name: Zambia
answers.fact: August 20, 1992: dedicated Zambia for the preaching of the gospel.

prompts.display_text: Pin a European country where World War I sent foreign missionaries home and local Saints carried on.
prompts.text_original: A European country where World War I (1914-18) forced the Church to evacuate, release or sharply reduce its foreign missionaries.
prompts.citation: Church History Department, Global Histories country chronologies, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: When World War I began in 1914, the Church pulled most American missionaries out of Europe. Local members kept branches alive, served as missionaries at home, and in Germany baptized more than 500 converts during the war.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: 1914-19: all North American missionaries left; local members served and baptized more than 500 converts.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: 1914-18: fewer American missionaries were called and local members began to serve as missionaries.

answers.name: Belgium
answers.fact: 1914-18: full-time missionaries were evacuated; Saints held sacrament meetings in homes.

answers.name: Switzerland
answers.fact: August 30, 1914, Basel: mission president Hyrum W. Valentine was told to release all missionaries.

answers.name: France
answers.fact: August 1914: the French Mission was absorbed into other missions and all missionaries left France.

answers.name: Netherlands
answers.fact: 1914-19: missionaries were reassigned to safer missions; local members were called to serve.

answers.name: Austria
answers.fact: August 1914: all missionaries in Austria were evacuated.

answers.name: Denmark
answers.fact: October 1914: many missionaries not native to Denmark were sent home.

answers.name: Hungary
answers.fact: August 10, 1914: the outbreak of war led to the evacuation of all missionaries.

answers.name: Iceland
answers.fact: 1914: as the war began, missionary work in Iceland was discontinued.

answers.name: Norway
answers.fact: 1914-18: fewer North American missionaries; local members became home missionaries.
